strings.investigation.pip_identity.title: The Little Ghost's Old Receipt
strings.investigation.pip_identity.hypothesis.ol: Pip has been coming to Moonmart for a very long time.
The receipt and photograph place Pip in the shop decades ago. The memory belongs to Pip, even if the name is still missing.
strings.investigation.pip_identity.hypothesis.or: The receipt must belong to a different customer.
It could be a mistake. Agnes suggests checking the old photograph before deciding.
strings.investigation.whisperwood_silence.title: Where the Birds Went
strings.investigation.whisperwood_silence.hypoth: The silence is moving through the old roots.
The quiet is traveling along roots that connect the grove to a forgotten shrine.
Fern agrees migration is possible, but the empty nests and quiet roots point somewhere else.
strings.investigation.lucien_and_ada.title: A Dedication in the Margins
Ada was Lucien's friend before his long life began.
The letter is an invitation to talk, not an attempt to take back the years.
The old book and Lucien's careful letter point to a friendship that mattered to him.
Lucien has kept the book and reached out gently. It suggests Ada mattered deeply, though only the two of them can say what their friendship means now.
strings.investigation.wren_sister.title: The Passenger Who Never Arrived
strings.investigation.wren_sister.hypothesis.sis: Wren's sister may still be travelling in the Between.
The family mark is recent enough to offer hope, but no one can promise where the train went.
strings.investigation.wren_sister.hypothesis.fam: The disappearing station on Wren's map may be linked to the ticket bearing her family mark.
The map and ticket point toward the same uncertain route. They give Wren somewhere to look, but they do not prove her sister is still aboard.
strings.investigation.long_midnight.title: A Night Missing from the Records
strings.investigation.long_midnight.hypothesis.s: The town forgot the Long Midnight together.
The missing street and missing date line up. The town's records were changed in the same quiet act of forgetting.
One ghost changed the photograph and map.
That could explain one photograph, but it cannot explain why the post office and old maps have the same blank space.
strings.investigation.osric_name.title: A Passenger Without a Name
strings.investigation.osric_name.hypothesis.name: Remembering Osric's name helps him stay present.
When the name is written down, Osric's outline grows a little clearer.
strings.investigation.osric_name.hypothesis.cond: The Conductor's memory may help keep Osric present when the town forgets him.
The Conductor remembers passengers the town has lost. That gives Osric another anchor, though his own memories are still incomplete.
strings.investigation.midnight_platform.title: The Station Between Stations
strings.investigation.midnight_platform.hypothes: The platform remembers passengers the town has forgotten.
The station keeps names safe until someone is ready to hear them again.
The Conductor's memories and the station between stops may serve the same lost passengers.

The Conductor remembers people the town has lost, and the platform sits between ordinary destinations. Together they suggest the station is a refuge for passengers in transit, though its full rules remain unknown.
strings.investigation.miso_guardian.title: The Cat Who Stayed
strings.investigation.miso_guardian.hypothesis.v: Miso stayed by choice, but can choose differently now.
Miso was a guardian, never a prisoner. The distinction matters.
strings.investigation.miso_guardian.hypothesis.m: The old photographs and Miso's lingering memory suggest the watch began as a choice.
The images suggest Miso chose to stay beside the doorway. They cannot tell us whether that choice still feels right, so the present choice belongs to Miso.
strings.investigation.lighthouse_beacon.title: What the Light Was For
strings.investigation.lighthouse_beacon.hypothes: The lighthouse guides lost travellers toward a safe crossing.
The light does not pull anyone across. It shows a way home to people who want one.
The beam's direction and restored light point to a safe route across the Between.
The beam crosses toward the Between, then marks a route home. That supports a guiding purpose, though it does not explain who first built the lighthouse.
strings.investigation.original_agreement.title: The Promise Under Moonmart
strings.investigation.original_agreement.hypothe: The old agreement asks for shelter, not sacrifice.
No one was bound to guard the doorway. The promise was simply that a light would be left on.
The Conductor's remembered promise supports the idea that Moonmart offered shelter by choice.
The old records and the Conductor's memory both describe a place kept for travellers. That points to shelter as the promise, though some details of the first agreement are still missing.
strings.investigation.boundary.title: How Bellwether Will Remember
strings.investigation.boundary.hypothesis.many_p: The boundary can change without erasing anyone's choice.
The future does not have to be the same door for everyone.
strings.investigation.boundary.hypothesis.miso_a: Miso's choice and the boundary's possible futures both respect a right to choose.
Miso's freedom and the boundary's possible futures share a principle of choice. That principle can guide the town, even though each traveller may want something different.
strings.investigation.harbour_wishes.title: A Small Wish for Safe Returns
The blue glass tokens are a small harbour custom for wishing boats a safe return.

The net-mender ties the blue bead beside the boat's little tag, keeping the old wish alive for whoever comes next. It does not explain where the empty boat travels, but it makes the harbour feel a little less lonely.
strings.investigation.harbour_night_boats.title: The Boats That Leave After Midnight
strings.investigation.harbour_night_boats.hypoth: The harbour's empty boats quietly carry small wishes out past the breakwater after midnight and return before dawn.
The oars, the warm lantern hook and the beads all describe the same gentle errand. The boats carry wishes outward and come home dry, and the net-mender has always known to leave them be.
Someone keeps a lantern watch so no traveller reaches an unlit harbour.
A warm lantern hook and gentle oars suggest a patient watch. The keeper is unseen, but the harbour is kept ready, and that is a comfort rather than a threat.
Smugglers must be using the quay after dark.
Nothing is ever missing and no crates are ever left behind. The oars sound more like a lullaby than a getaway. Look for what the boats are carrying instead.
strings.investigation.whisperwood_shifting_paths: The shifting paths are the wood's way of guiding lost visitors gently back toward the grove.
The flowers lean and the roots point, and the way out is always among them. Whisperwood rearranges itself to help, never to keep anyone.
The ribbons are route markers left by someone who walks the wood to help wanderers.
The knots match the trails the flowers point along. Someone patient has been quietly leaving a thread of kindness, though Fern says she has never met them.
The wood shifts its paths to keep visitors from leaving.
The paths never close behind anyone, and the moonflowers always lean toward the way out. Fern would say the wood is shy, not hungry.
strings.investigation.unclaimed_drawer.title: The Drawer Marked Unclaimed
strings.investigation.unclaimed_drawer.hypothesi: The Unclaimed drawer shelters the names of people the town has not yet remembered.
Each card waits quietly until someone speaks its name, and then it fills in. The drawer is not a grave but a resting place, and it is open to anyone who wants to lend a name.
Lost names find their way home through the post and the archive's cards together.
A card in the drawer and an envelope in the tray name the same person. The town has two quiet ways of holding a name until its owner is ready, though neither will say who set them going.
Juniper must be forgetting things she wrote herself.
Juniper remembers everything she has ever been told. The cards are extra, not missing, and she is doing what the town cannot yet do. Look at what happens when a card is named.

strings.companion.dream.heading: A DREAM WITH MISO
strings.companion.dream.beat.lamp_room.title: The little lamp
strings.companion.dream.beat.lamp_room.text: You stand in Moonmart before the shop was yours. Rain whispers at the window, and a small lamp keeps one circle of gold on the counter. Miso waits beside it, looking as old as the hills.
strings.companion.dream.beat.threshold.title: The blue doorway
strings.companion.dream.beat.threshold.text: Miso leads you to a blue doorway where the shop wall should be. A brass bell sways there without a sound. Beyond it, rain falls upward into a patient silver sky.
strings.companion.dream.beat.ledger.title: A page left open
strings.companion.dream.beat.ledger.text: The old ledger lies open, its ink changing like reflections in a puddle. Beside it sits a cup gone cold and a note written in a hand you almost remember.
strings.companion.dream.beat.dawn.title: A quiet morning
strings.companion.dream.beat.dawn.text: The dream gathers itself around a small kindness. The lamp is still warm. Miso's purr becomes the sound of rain returning to the right side of the window.
strings.companion.dream.choice.follow_miso: Follow Miso to the blue doorway
strings.companion.dream.choice.read_margin: Read the note in the ledger margin
strings.companion.dream.choice.leave_page: Leave the page open for someone
strings.companion.dream.choice.keep_warmth: Keep the warmth of the lamp
strings.companion.dream.response.follow_miso: Miso looks back to be sure you are following. The doorway opens onto a memory without asking you to name it.
strings.companion.dream.response.listen_to_kettl: A kettle hums though the fire is out. Its gentle note carries you toward a page left open on the counter.
strings.companion.dream.response.touch_bell: The bell warms beneath your hand. Somewhere far away, a door is held open for a traveler.
strings.companion.dream.response.watch_rain: Each silver drop catches a tiny reflection of the shop. Miso blinks, and the rain carries you onward.
strings.companion.dream.response.read_margin: The note says only, 'There will always be a light on.' The words settle softly into the paper.
strings.companion.dream.response.leave_page: You leave the note for whoever needs it next. Miso curls beside the ledger, keeping its place.
strings.companion.dream.response.keep_warmth: You carry a little of the lamp's warmth with you. It asks nothing in return.
strings.companion.dream.response.keep_quiet: You carry the sound of Miso's purr, steady as a promise made without words.
strings.companion.dream.suspend_hint: You can step away and return to this dream later.
strings.companion.dream.wake_message: Miso wakes with a quiet purr. The dream stays with you as a small, optional memory.

strings.companion.memory_echo.platform_lamp.text: A much younger Miso sits beneath the station lamp after the last train. When a frightened traveler steps down alone, Miso walks beside them all the way to a warm, open door.
strings.companion.memory_echo.the_last_train.tex: A conductor counts the empty seats twice. Miso watches from the windowsill, then nudges a folded blanket toward the passenger who stayed behind to help.
strings.companion.memory_echo.names_in_rain.text: Rain taps the old manifest while Miso listens to each name. One by one, every traveler answers from somewhere safe.

strings.interaction.cat_bed: Miso curls up beneath the warm lamp, paws tucked in.
strings.interaction.waiting_bench: The bench has room for two. You rest for a moment; the station clock waits with you.
strings.shift.message.begin: Night {night} begins. The shop is open; take your time.
strings.interaction.shop_quiet: The shop hums softly around you.
strings.interaction.register.ready: The register is ready. A little bell waits beside it.
strings.dawn.spoiled_goods.plural: {count} perishable items went past their best-before night.
strings.dawn.spoiled_goods.singular: {count} perishable item went past its best-before night.
strings.shift.message.minimum_service: Moonmart's promise asks for {minimum} minutes of open service first. {remaining} minute{plural} remain; unfinished stories will wait safely for another night.
strings.interaction.backroom.not_ready: The back room is still being tidied. Miso watches the doorway.
strings.dawn.shift_complete: Dawn settles over Bellwether. Night {night} is complete. Coins earned: {coins} · Moon Tokens earned: {moons}. Press {interact} to begin the next night.
strings.event.miso_purrs.message: Miso purrs beneath the counter, and the little shop feels warmer for it.
strings.event.window_rain.message: Rain threads silver lines down the window.
strings.event.flicker_lights.message: The lights dim. For a moment, a second moon hangs beyond the glass.
strings.event.receipt_whispers.message: A receipt rustles although the register is closed.
strings.event.receipt_whispers.investigation_pro: A faint name is caught between the totals. You can inspect the receipt at the register if you like.
strings.event.receipt_whispers.investigation_res: The receipt remembers a traveller who once needed a warm place to wait. A small forgotten token slips free: {amount} {currency}.
strings.event.bell_no_customer.message: The door bell rings. Nobody is there, but the shop feels a little less lonely.
strings.event.pastry_delivery.message: Agnes has left a paper bag of warm pastries.
strings.event.fern_birds.message: Fern says the birds have begun to sing at dawn again.
strings.event.lucien_rain.message: Lucien arrives early to escape the rain, carrying a book with a familiar inscription.
strings.event.platform_ticket.message: A damp railway ticket appears beneath the till. The destination has been rubbed away.
strings.event.lighthouse_glimmer.message: A pale beam crosses the shop window from the direction of the abandoned lighthouse.
strings.event.forgotten_receipt.message: The receipt printer produces a list of names, including one that nobody in town remembers.
strings.event.morning_birds.message: Somewhere beyond the shutters, morning birds begin their ordinary song.
strings.event.festival_spring_bloom.message: Neighbours leave small flowers outside Moonmart. By midnight, the whole square smells of rain and new leaves.
strings.event.festival_spring_rain.message: A procession of paper lanterns passes the window, each one carrying a wish written in careful ink.
strings.event.festival_summer_firefly.message: Fireflies gather above the harbour path. Miso watches their lights travel across the window glass.
strings.event.festival_summer_tide.message: The Long Tide Market begins after midnight. Somewhere outside, a boat bell answers the music.
strings.event.festival_autumn_harvest.message: A shared harvest table appears in the square, with a place set for anyone who arrives late.
strings.event.festival_autumn_veil.message: Bellwether lights small lamps for people far away. The glow rests gently along the edge of the Between.
strings.event.festival_winter_lantern.message: Warm lanterns bloom in every shop window. Even the snow looks softer beneath their light.
strings.event.festival_winter_stillness.message: The town grows quiet together. For a few minutes, everyone can hear the snow settle on the roofs.
strings.event.rain_on_brass.message: Rain taps softly on the brass bell above the shop door.
strings.event.fog_on_the_glass.message: A pale curl of fog gathers on the outer edge of the window, then thins.
strings.event.winter_window_tea.message: A cup warms your hands while the snow quiets the street outside.
strings.event.agnes_bread_basket.message: Agnes leaves a little basket of day-old rolls for anyone who needs one.
strings.event.fern_seed_envelopes.message: Fern tucks a few wildflower seeds beside the till, each one wrapped in a leaf.
strings.event.lucien_bookmark.message: Lucien returns a book with a pressed violet between its pages.
strings.event.mara_unsent_letters.message: Mara brings a bundle of letters that never found their addresses, and asks you to keep them safe.
strings.event.wren_moonflower_petal.message: Wren finds a silver petal on the counter and folds it inside her notebook.
strings.event.elias_shore_glass.message: Elias sets a piece of sea glass on the counter; the restored light made it shine at the shore.
strings.event.second_moon_reflection.message: The window reflection shows two moons for a heartbeat, then only one.
strings.event.ticket_stub_in_the_till.message: A ticket stub waits in the till. Its date is tomorrow, though the ink is decades old.
strings.event.winter_lantern_wick.message: Agnes brings a spare lantern wick and asks you to pass it to anyone walking home late.
strings.event.wind_chime_in_the_aisle.message: A soft chime sounds from the empty aisle, though every window is closed.
strings.event.autumn_shared_loaf.message: Agnes cuts a warm loaf into small pieces so the late visitors can share it.
strings.event.morning_after_the_boundary.message: The first ordinary birdcall reaches the shop, and everyone lets it finish before speaking.
strings.event.quiet_stamp_marks.message: A neat row of tiny crescent stamps appears on the paper bags. Nobody remembers bringing a stamp pad.
strings.event.fern_pocket_mint.message: Fern brings a sprig of mint from the grove and leaves it beside the kettle for tomorrow.
strings.event.lucien_two_chapter_note.message: Lucien returns a borrowed novel with a note tucked between two chapters: “I would like to hear what you think comes next.”
strings.event.wren_ticket_fold.message: Wren folds a fresh rubbing of the family mark and asks you to keep it with the other ticket clues.
strings.event.elias_low_tide.message: Elias describes the path the tide left below the lighthouse: smooth stones, small pools, and no hurry to cross them.
strings.event.mara_archive_label.message: Mara brings a new archive label that reads “places people may name for themselves.” She asks you to keep a few by the ledger.
strings.event.conductor_empty_platform.message: The Conductor says the platform was quiet tonight. No one was waiting, and that was a good thing.
strings.event.osric_quay_map.message: Osric draws the way from Moonmart to the quay on a scrap of paper, then adds a little blue house at the end.
strings.event.winter_salt_on_the_step.message: Someone has scattered a little salt across the shop step before the snow could freeze there.
strings.event.spring_seedling_shadow.message: A seedling's shadow reaches across the counter, though the pot is much too small to cast one that long.
strings.event.summer_harbor_salt.message: A clean salt-air smell drifts through the shop when the harbor breeze turns inland.
strings.event.autumn_jar_labels.message: Agnes brings a sheet of handwritten labels for the preserves. Each jar gets its own date and the name of the person who made it.
strings.event.saturday_paper_bag.message: Agnes leaves a paper bag by the register with two rolls: one for the shop and one for whoever needs supper.
strings.event.miso_cardboard_crescent.message: Miso has settled into an empty delivery box and is looking out through a crescent-shaped tear.
strings.event.aftermarket_bus_schedule.message: A late bus schedule is pinned beside the door. Someone has circled the stop closest to home.
strings.event.lunar_sugar_spoon.message: A little crescent of sugar has collected in the teaspoon, though the jar lid is closed.
strings.event.agnes_oven_timer.message: Agnes says the old oven timer rang once at home, though nothing was baking. She laughs and says the shop is teaching it patience.
strings.event.fern_spiderweb_sunrise.message: Fern describes a spiderweb in the restored grove that held the first light like a tiny, careful map.
strings.event.lucien_library_ribbon.message: Lucien says the library has added a ribbon to the shelf of books with happy endings. He looks mildly surprised that the shelf is getting crowded.
strings.event.wren_constellation_outline.message: Wren sketches a constellation she and her sister used to look for. One star is missing from the drawing, but she leaves space for it.
strings.event.mara_return_address.message: Mara finds a return address printed in an old typeface: “To the place that keeps a light on.” She adds it to the archive without guessing who sent it.
strings.event.elias_shutter_check.message: Elias checks the shop's latch against the wind and says the lighthouse shutters needed the same little adjustment every winter.
strings.event.pip_strawberry_ring.message: A pink ring of condensation appears beneath the strawberry milk bottle, then fades before it reaches the receipt.
strings.event.osric_blue_roof.message: Osric remembers that his sister used to paint the little blue house roof after the first spring rain. He says he may visit the quay when the day comes.
strings.event.conductor_watch_still.message: The Conductor's pocket watch has stopped, but this time he does not wind it. He says the passengers have enough time.
strings.event.sunday_pavement_chalk.message: Someone has drawn little arrows in chalk along the pavement, all pointing toward the well-lit street home.
strings.event.tide_table_on_the_wall.message: A hand-copied tide table has appeared beside the noticeboard, with the safest harbour crossing circled twice.
strings.event.spring_violet_unfurls.message: One violet on the garden shelf opens just enough to show its pale centre, then settles back into the leaves.
strings.event.quiet_train_whistle.message: A distant train whistle reaches the shop through the fog. It sounds like an invitation, not a warning.
strings.event.first_post_covenant.message: A postcard arrives with no return address. It says only: “We found the way home. Thank you for leaving the light on.”
strings.event.fern_roof_garden_cuttings.message: Fern leaves a jar of roof-garden cuttings by the back door, with a note about which ones like the morning shade.
strings.event.agnes_shared_recipe_card.message: Agnes writes her simple oat-biscuit recipe on the back of a grocery list and says it belongs to anyone who needs it.
strings.event.lucien_library_return_slot.message: Lucien mentions the library has kept its return slot open late for night-shift workers. He seems pleased that the books keep finding their way home.
strings.event.wren_stationery_star_map.message: Wren draws a small star map on a scrap of paper and leaves the lower corner blank for a place she has not found yet.
strings.event.mara_old_postmark.message: Mara shows you a letter with a postmark from a street that no longer appears on the town map. She files it under “still remembered.”
strings.event.elias_lighthouse_lunch_tin.message: Elias brings back the old lunch tin he used at the lighthouse. He says the dent on its lid came from a very ordinary windy Tuesday.
strings.event.osric_quay_bench_repaired.message: Osric says someone has repaired the loose board on the quay bench. He remembers sitting there after school, though the name of his school has not come back yet.
strings.event.conductor_platform_clock.message: The Conductor says a clock on the platform has begun keeping ordinary time again. Nobody needs to hurry because of it.
strings.event.pip_receipt_sunshine.message: A narrow stripe of moonlight rests across the receipt roll. Pip says it looks a little like a sunny place from a dream.
strings.event.shop_bell_windless_chime.message: The brass bell above the door gives one soft note on a still night. The note fades before anyone reaches for the handle.
strings.event.cold_shelf_frost_pattern.message: A little frost draws a fern shape on the outside of the cold cabinet, then melts where the shop is warmest.
strings.event.garden_shelf_moonmoth.message: A pale moth rests on a leaf by the garden shelf. It stays just long enough for the kettle to click off.
strings.event.rainy_boots_by_the_door.message: A pair of muddy boots has been left neatly beside the mat. By the next blink, the footprints have dried away.
strings.event.harbour_rope_knots.message: A short length of clean rope lies coiled beside the noticeboard, tied in the same patient knot used on harbour nets.
strings.event.late_bus_warm_lamp.message: The last bus pauses beneath the streetlamp outside. No one gets off, but its warm windows make the wet pavement feel less empty.
strings.event.open_door_mixed_market.message: A note from Agnes describes neighbours from both sides of the boundary sharing tea and ordinary stories at a market table.
strings.event.keeper_late_sanctuary.message: The Conductor leaves a note by the bell: Moonmart's light remains a safe place to pause between journeys.
strings.event.gentle_goodbye_memory_letters.mess: A letter from Lucien arrives by post. Its old visitor's story finds a place in the journal, where the closed doorway cannot erase it.
strings.event.spring_names_on_the_window.message: Spring rain gathers on the glass and, for a moment, the drops run together into a name you almost remember.
strings.event.spring_promise_seed_jar.message: Fern leaves a jar of seeds by the till with a label in green ink: a promise to plant them when the first warm night arrives.
strings.event.spring_fog_forgotten_doorstep.mess: Through the spring fog, a figure pauses at the doorstep, looks at the lit window as if reading a half-remembered book, and drifts gently on.
strings.event.summer_firefly_memory_jar.message: A firefly drifts in behind a customer and settles in an empty jar, where it glows like a small remembered afternoon.
strings.event.summer_tide_whisper_shell.message: A pale shell on the counter hums with the sound of the harbour. If you listen closely, it seems to say your name kindly.
strings.event.summer_harbour_night_market.messag: Lanterns bob at the harbour end of the street, and somewhere a vendor you cannot see is selling cold lemonade to the moon.
strings.event.autumn_leaf_with_a_name.message: The wind carries one amber leaf through the door. A name is written across it in fine silver script, and it settles gently by the register.
strings.event.autumn_lantern_loaf.message: Agnes brings a round loaf stamped with a little lantern. She says it is for whoever has walked the longest to get here tonight.
strings.event.autumn_veil_ink_blot.message: Mara leaves a page where the ink has bled into a soft map of streets that are not yet written down. She asks you to keep it dry.
strings.event.winter_snow_remembers_footsteps.me: Fresh snow settles on the step, and for a moment a line of footprints appears in it, pointing in from long ago, then fills quietly in.
strings.event.winter_promise_mittens.message: Osric leaves a pair of mittens on the counter, knitted in the blue of his old roof. He says they belong to whoever promised to come back.
strings.event.winter_tea_corner_steam.message: In the Tea Corner, a cup nobody poured breathes out a curl of steam shaped like a small, contented cat.
strings.event.greenhouse_midnight_bloom.message: Inside the Greenhouse, a single moonflower opens a few minutes early and fills the glass with a hush like held breath.
strings.event.reading_nook_borrowed_hours.messag: Lucien leaves a note in the Reading Nook: he has marked a chair for any visitor who wants to borrow an hour from the rain.
strings.event.memory_wall_soft_glow.message: On the Between room's memory wall, one small frame glows softly, as if a forgotten afternoon has remembered how to be a keepsake.
strings.event.pip_name_on_the_ledger.message: Pip writes a name carefully in the corner of the ledger, then looks up, delighted. The ink does not fade, and neither does he.
strings.event.platform_unclaimed_umbrella.messag: The Conductor hangs an unclaimed umbrella by the door and says it belongs to someone the Between has not finished remembering.
strings.interaction.inspect.nothing_unusual: Nothing unusual catches your eye. You can come back to this when you know more.
strings.interaction.reading_nook.read: You settle in with a book. The quiet makes room for the next thought.
strings.interaction.reading_nook.rest: You rest in the reading nook for a moment. There is no hurry to leave.
strings.interaction.greenhouse.plants.inspect: Moonlit leaves shelter seeds, herbs, and ingredients gathered for the shop.
strings.interaction.greenhouse.plants.water: You water the seedlings. Their leaves settle softly beneath the glass.
strings.interaction.greenhouse.plants.already_wa: The moon herbs and seedlings have already been watered this shift.
strings.interaction.greenhouse.trellis: A moonflower vine climbs the trellis. Anouk's tag says its leaves close gently before dawn.
strings.decoration.message.moon_jasmine: Moon jasmine petals tilt toward the window. Silver veins form a tiny line: Even a quiet light can help someone find the way home.
strings.decoration.message.moon_jasmine_repeat: The moon jasmine has already shared its small message. Its petals rest quietly.
strings.housekeeping.result.wipe_counter: The counter is clear and smooth under the lamp.
strings.housekeeping.result.sweep_floor: Leaves and tracked-in dust are swept away.
strings.housekeeping.result.water_plants: The shop plants settle after a gentle drink.
strings.housekeeping.result.clear_cups: Clean cups are ready for the next late-night tea.
strings.housekeeping.result.take_out_rubbish: The rubbish is outside, and the back room can breathe.
strings.housekeeping.result.refill_dispenser: The canisters are full and ready for another quiet night.
